summary: Union-Wallowa fire lookout on Mount Emily, Union County: cupola cabin 1916, 81 ft steel tower 1926, used for emergencies into the 1960s; now gone per the register.

facts.status_note: Register says the tower is now gone; firelookout.com says it has long since departed.

access.note: Union County runs the Mount Emily Recreation Area (MERA) as a multi-use recreation area. No source says whether the old lookout site is inside it.

corrections.why: The register describes an 81-foot steel tower built in 1926, which is 24.7 m. The 12.2 m (40 ft) figure matches the 40-foot tower a local paper proposed in 1916 rather than the tower that was built.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register describes an 81-foot steel tower from 1926. A 1916 newspaper item proposed a 40-foot tower. The story and facts use the built tower's 81 feet.

A state forestry report, under its 1914 entries, describes a five-mile line built to the lookout point. A 1915 La Grande Observer item says it was constructed during 1913 and is about six miles long. The story gives the 1914 report's account and notes the 1915 item.

notes_for_editor: The brief height (12.2 m) is corrected above. The weebly history mentions a Blumenstein cabin at the lookout headquarters in 1914, before the 1916 cupola, so 1916 is not the first building on the site. The firelookout.com 1958 name is the last known lookout. No source read says what remains on the summit or whether the old lookout site is open; MERA's page gives no location detail. The WWNF record could not be checked against the FFLOS detail page beyond the registration date.
